reading.body:
Centeris operates the South Hill campus, an 86-acre private data center facility near Puyallup in the Greater Seattle region, with 24 megawatts of published power infrastructure. At a typical AI training density of 40 kilowatts per rack, 24 megawatts of IT load would support roughly 600 racks, though the operator's own spec does not break down IT load, PUE, or the split between colocation and reserved capacity. The facility is the second-largest published data center campus in Washington state by power, behind one other mapped facility, in a state where only two of 46 mapped facilities publish power figures.

The research note confirms Centeris as the operator and South Hill as the campus name, verifies The Benaroya Company, a Pacific Northwest real estate firm, as 100 percent owner, and identifies the facility as a colocation campus, but no street address is published on the operator's own site. The operator's site provides only a corporate office address in Bellevue, roughly 30 miles away. A third-party listing names a different operator, Colocation Northwest, for a same-named South Hill facility at a Puyallup address, but neither operator's published site confirms any relationship, so that address is not applied here.

No certifications, power purchase agreements, renewable energy claims, grid interconnection details, or colocation pricing terms are published on the operator's site. The 24-megawatt figure alone does not indicate whether the campus is constrained by power delivery, whether it serves AI workloads, or how much of its capacity is currently in use.
